_README: Per-million-token prices, each stamped with the date it was read off the
vendor's own pricing page. cost_ledger.Rate.is_stale() flags anything older
than the configured window, because a ceiling computed from unchecked prices
These are STANDARD tier, prompts under 200k tokens. Batch, flex, and priority
tiers differ; so does long-context pricing above 200k. If a run ever sends a
prompt over 200k tokens these numbers are wrong and the ceiling is too loose.
Re-check every 90 days. Vendors change prices without notice.

seat_1._note_max_input_tokens: Largest request this price was checked for, from the vendor's own documentation. null means unchecked: a larger request is still authorised and the report says so. Fill it in yourself; a guessed limit is a guessed ceiling.
seat_1._note_tiers: Optional [[min_input_tokens, input_per_mtok, output_per_mtok], ...] for providers that charge more above a context threshold. Without it every call is priced at the standard tier, which under-charges the ones that cross it.
seat_1._note_output_multiplier: Billed output as a multiple of max_tokens. Measured 0.24x on a live canary at production caps; set to 2.0 for headroom. A call that bills more than it was authorised for halts the run, so an optimistic value is caught on first use rather than at the end of the bill. Raise it if you see an overrun; lower it once you have runs of your own to calibrate against.

seat_2._note_output_multiplier: Billed output as a multiple of max_tokens. MEASURED TWICE AND THE SECOND FIGURE BROKE THE FIRST BOUND: 1.23x on an early canary, then 2.9x on the first five-round run, whose round-one prompt is longer. At 2.5 that call billed $0.1475 against $0.1289 authorised and the overrun halt correctly stopped the run two calls in. Set to 6.0, keeping this file's own convention of roughly doubling the largest measurement for headroom. This seat needs the most of any: Gemini bills thinking tokens that max_output_tokens does not bound, and the OpenAI-compatibility layer silently ignores parameters it does not list, so the cap is a request rather than a limit.
